summary: This note is the Snowflake documentation page for the ALTER DATABASE ROLE SQL command, which modifies properties of an existing database role. The only supported operations are renaming a database role and adding, overwriting, or removing a comment, plus setting and unsetting tags. It lists the syntax, parameters, the OWNERSHIP and APPLY privileges required, a metadata usage caution, and two examples (a rename and adding a comment).
one_line: Snowflake reference for the ALTER DATABASE ROLE command, covering renaming, comments, tags, required privileges and examples.
key_facts: ALTER DATABASE ROLE modifies the properties for an existing database role.
Currently the only supported operations are renaming a database role or adding, overwriting, or removing a comment for a database role.
The syntax includes IF EXISTS, RENAME TO <new_name>, SET COMMENT, UNSET COMMENT, SET TAG, and UNSET TAG.
The <name> identifier must be unique in the database in which the role is created.
An identifier must start with an alphabetic character and cannot contain spaces or special characters unless enclosed in double quotes.
Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are case-sensitive.
If the identifier is not fully qualified as db_name.database_role_name, the command looks for the database role in the current database for the session.
When renaming a fully-qualified database role, the database name must remain the same; only database_role_name can change.
The new_name for RENAME TO must be unique for the account.
The tag value is always a string with a maximum of 256 characters.
Executing this command requires the OWNERSHIP privilege on the database role, and only the owner or a higher role can execute it.
The owner role does not inherit permissions granted to the owned database role.
The APPLY privilege on a Tag enables setting a tag on a database role.
Example: ALTER DATABASE ROLE d1.dr1 RENAME TO d1.dbr2 renames database role dr1 to dbr2 in database d1.
Example: ALTER DATABASE ROLE d1.dbr2 SET COMMENT = 'New comment for database role' adds a comment to d1.dbr2.
